cit.q: from the man from a land of close-set(?) mountains
this good village of fields with cotton hedges
paṉṉalam pañcik kuṉṟam paṭar eri mukantat' oppa
so as to resemble a spreading flame engulfing a mountain of cotton for hand-tousing

sense.note: The verb paṉṉutal as such is hardly attested in the early corpus, and its meaning can only be derived from the rare occurrences of the verbal noun that deal with the processing for cotton. The only early passage in the is unfortunately so elliptical that no precise meaning can be given. The verb becomes standard when used inside an extended metaphor for textual production (see meaning 2).

This word is an isolated occurrence in the old corpus but the interpretation of “cotton” is backed up by three things. Firstly, in the formulaic system connected with vēli (“fence” or “hedge”) paṉṉal can be replaced with parutti (as in PN 299.1, 324.7). Secondly, the Nikaṇṭu-s enumerates paṉṉal as one of the words for parutti (see below). Thirdly, etymologically it is tempting to explain paṉṉal as a verbal noun belonging to a verb paṉṉutal, to weave (DEDR 4207). The TL even lists as the first meaning of that verb “to touse with the fingers, as cotton”.

At least one further passage suggests that the noun does not refer simply to the cotton plant but cotton in some processed form, unclear which exactly as long as the verb paṉṉutal (separated by the DEDR in two entries, namely 4207 and 3887) is not understood more precisely as to its technical implications (tousing?, spinning?, weaving?). This is confirmed by the cognate paṉuval, another type of verbal noun, presumably of the same verb but with a single ṉ, which may refer to a product made of cotton (compared in NA 353.1-3 to the clouds gathering on a mountain).

cit.q: val toṇṭaṉ | paṉṉu tamiḻ nūl mālai vallār
those who master the garland [made] according to the Tamil treatises composed by the harsh devotee
those who master the garland [made] according to the Tamil treatises composed by Kulacēkaraṉ

sense.note: Note that the verb comes up with the bhakti corpus and both by Śaivas and by Vaiṣṇavas is used with preference in the signature verses that deal with the crafting of poetry/song.
